title: Automation & agents
summary: Run agent work as an auditable engineering workflow: understand, plan, review, apply, build, fix, and deliver.

sections.heading: Agent workflow
body: Velclaw combines repository-aware agents, isolated workspaces, Git automation, pull requests, review, and deployment control behind one workflow.
A useful execution sequence is Understand → Plan → Review → Apply → Build → Fix. Each stage should expose enough state for a person to inspect what happened.

sections.heading: Give agents project context
body: Agent work should be connected to the actual project context instead of relying on an isolated prompt. This reduces ambiguity and makes the resulting change easier to review.

sections.heading: Validation gates
body: Treat agent output as normal engineering work. Inspect the diff, run the repository validation commands, review security-sensitive changes, and only then advance to delivery.
For autonomous workflows, runtime verification, security/configuration audit, documentation synchronization, and product QA are explicit stages rather than hidden assumptions.

sections.heading: Skills and integrations
body: Velclaw includes agent-facing tooling and configuration surfaces, while MCP and skills can extend the available workflow. Keep permissions scoped to the task and avoid exposing credentials to untrusted execution.
